Which of the following statements are true concerning the function $y=f(x)$ whose graph is shown above? 

I. ${lim}_{x\to \,0}f(x)=\text{DNE}$

II. ${lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=2$

III. ${lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)={lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)$
question.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. As $x$ approaches $0$ from the left and right we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{0}^{-}}f(x)=0,\,{lim}_{x\to \,{0}^{+}}f(x)=1\,.
$$

 
Therefore, ${lim}_{x\to \,{0}^{-}}f(x)\ne {lim}_{x\to \,{0}^{+}}f(x),$ and hence ${lim}_{x\to \,0}f(x)=\text{DNE}.$

- Statement II is false. As $x$ approaches $1$ from the left and right we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{-}}f(x)=2,\,{lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}f(x)=\text{DNE}\,.
$$

 
Therefore, ${lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{-}}f(x)\ne {lim}_{x\to \,{1}^{+}}f(x),$ and hence ${lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=\text{DNE}.$

- Statement III is false. We see from the graph that 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=\text{DNE},\,{lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)=\text{DNE}
$$

 We can't say that the limits are equal because we can't compare undefined values.

In conclusion, only statement I is true.
